start.text: The club room is dark. Maya sits on the floor, back against the bookshelf, her poetry notebook open in her lap. She doesn't look up when {player_name} comes in.

n1.text: I read you the last line yesterday, didn't I? I read to the walls a lot, sometimes I mix them up.

n2.text: You know what's worse? This morning I woke up without remembering my dream, for the first time in a hundred loops. And I missed it.

b1.text: He had a scar on his chin. From a bike. He said it was from fighting a shark. I laughed every time, even knowing it was a lie.

b2.text: Thank you. I've never told anyone that. Now someone else knows about the scar.

b3.text: ...Love him. You said it in front of me as if it were something possible to say. No one ever has.

b4.text: Okay. I'll try not to remember his face today. Just the love. That seems to be the lighter part.

n3.text: I missed the nightmare. It was the only thing that let me see his face.
choices: Sit beside her and ask her to describe his face.
Say she doesn't need to remember his face to love him.

start.text: The hallways are empty. At the end of the second floor, a single light is on. Maya is there, leaning on the window, counting the courtyard lamps like someone praying.

n1.text: Four of them have gone out by themselves since yesterday. I know them. They belonged to the students in 2-C.

n2.text: I did this, didn't I? When I think about letting go, the world collects. I let go half a centimeter and a third of the class disappeared.

b1.text: A real promise? The kind that hurts? Then give me your hand. At least so I know the hand exists.

b2.text: I'm not? I've been guilty for so long. I don't know how to be anything else. But I can try not being it for a few minutes.

n3.text: I don't want you to forgive me. I want you to stop me from doing it again, if I try to hold on one more day.
choices: Promise you'll stop her.
Say none of this is her fault.

start.text: The white lantern hangs on the last string in the courtyard, alone, unlit. Maya stares at it with an unstruck match between her fingers.

n1.text: I made it on day 5. I wrote his name inside, with the tip of the pen, so it wouldn't show. A name no one knows.

n2.text: Tomorrow I'll light it. I wanted you to choose the time. I don't know how to choose times. I only know how to count up to them.

b1.text: Before the fireworks. Deal. Write it on your hand so I won't forget, because I'm good at counting and terrible at remembering.

b2.text: When the time comes. You're giving the choice back to me. No one ever has. Thank you. I'll know, when it comes.

n3.text: It could be before the first star. Or after the fireworks. Or never, and we leave it like that, beautiful, unlit.
choices: Choose to light it before the fireworks.
Leave the decision to her, when the time comes.

start.text: The sun is almost down. Maya waits at the foot of the roof stairs, in uniform, holding the unlit white lantern in both hands.

n1.text: When we go up, I'll tell you the last thing. Before that, I wanted to thank you, here, where no one's looking.

n2.text: You showed up on the first day as if it were the first time, and it was the first time anyone looked at me without wanting me to be okay.

b1.text: No. Going up first is what I've always done. This time we go up together. One step at a time.

b2.text: ...As long as I need. You know I might need one minute or a hundred loops?

b3.text: Then it's one minute. Just one. I already know what to do with it.

n3.text: I'm scared. I'm very scared. But I'm scared the right way: like someone about to do something that matters.
choices: "I'll go up first. Come when you're ready."
"I'll stay here with you as long as you need."

start.text: Yuna is in an apron, alone in the club kitchen, flour even in her hair. There are three cookie trays on the table, each with one extra star cut out.

n1.text: I know, I know! I make too much. But today it's on purpose. Today I know who it's for.

n2.text: It's for the neighbor who laughed before saying something silly. I don't remember his name. I remember how he broke the cookie in half and gave me the bigger piece.

b1.text: ...It is? Really? I make them from memory, no recipe. Can you taste him in it?

b2.text: I can. It tastes like summer. Like his house. Like an afternoon that never ended.

b3.text: Oh, stop! You'll make me cry into the dough. Have another. There's always one left over.

n3.text: I thought if I made the right recipe, he'd show up. Like a spell. Silly, right?
choices: Taste the cookie and say it's just like the ones he made.
Say it isn't silly and eat the cookie with her.

start.text: The classroom is empty. Yuna sits at a desk in the back with a recipe book open, lightly drawing faces over each recipe.

n1.text: The lunch lady disappeared. Mei disappeared. Mr. Takeda, who stood at the entrance. I'm drawing them so I won't forget.

n2.text: I draw badly. But a crooked face is better than no face. I'm good at making what's left look pretty.

b1.text: Okay. Hold still. I'll draw your weird nose and your hair that never stays down. I'll draw it just right.

b2.text: You'd do that? Come after me? Every loop? ...Then I won't disappear. I'll leave a trail of cookie crumbs, like Hansel and Gretel.

n3.text: I'm afraid I'll be next. That I'll wake up and no one will remember I existed. Like the... the boy with the bike.
choices: Ask her to draw you too, so she remembers.
Say that if she disappears, he'll look for her in every loop.

start.text: The festival stage is set up, with a microphone, cables and cellophane spotlights. Yuna rehearses alone, her back to the empty audience, singing softly.

n1.text: I sang this song at my elementary school graduation. There was a boy in the audience, in the back row, who kept clapping alone after everyone stopped.

n2.text: I thought it was embarrassing and beautiful. I want to sing for that boy tomorrow. Even if he isn't there.

b1.text: Deal! And if you cry, I'll pretend I didn't see. If I cry, you pretend too, okay? That's the deal.

b2.text: Yuna's voice fills the empty stage, small and steady. At the end of the verse, somewhere behind the curtain, someone claps once, slowly.

b3.text: ...Did you hear that? I did. It wasn't you. You were in front. Oh my God.

n3.text: Will you clap when I finish? Just you, in the back, after everyone stops?
choices: Promise to clap alone, after everyone else.
Ask her to sing it for him now, just one verse.

start.text: The courtyard is packed, but Yuna pulls him by the sleeve behind the stage, where no one can see. She's holding two lunchboxes. Her hand is ice cold.

n1.text: I made yours, and his. I know I shouldn't, but I wanted to leave one on the desk on day 13, just to be sure there is a day 13.

b1.text: Okay. I'll keep your lunch warm. I'm good at that. I know how to keep food and hopes wrapped in a dish towel.

b2.text: ...Thank you for not lying. Everyone lies to me so I won't cry. You're the first who respects me enough to let me cry.

n2.text: Promise you'll come back? It's not for me. It's so I have someone coming back. I take care of everyone, but I've never had someone who came back.
choices: "I'll come back. I promise, and I keep my promises."
"I don't know if I'll come back. But I'll try."

start.text: Alice has spread the notebook, the watch, the cut yearbook and the enrollment list across the desk, forming a kind of map. She stands with her arms crossed, looking down at it all.

n1.text: I built the timeline. Three apparent weeks. Twelve real days. Fifty-seven previous loops, by my calculations, with a margin of error of forty.

n2.text: The only constant in every loop is you. The second constant is me, writing things down without remembering I wrote them.

b1.text: Here. Page fourteen: "He always arrives with the same expression of someone who forgot something important." I wrote that forty times.

b2.text: ...If I'm okay. No one ever asked, in any of the fifty-seven. I am. Almost. Thank you for asking.

n3.text: That means that, even forgetting, I always trusted you. It's the only thing that needs no proof.
choices: Thank her, and ask to see the whole notebook.
Ask if she's okay being the mind of the loop.

start.text: Alice sits on the hallway floor, her notebook open upright against her knees. She writes something, erases it, and writes again.

n1.text: Probability that the next loop preserves my memory: two percent. Probability that I keep being me: ninety-one.

n2.text: It's curious. I accept losing my memory. What scares me is no longer wanting to know.

b1.text: Noted: he promised. Also noted: I believed him. Both, in the same handwriting.

b2.text: ...Deserve. I've never used that word with my curiosity. I'll test it. One hour. Timed.

n3.text: If I forget, tell me the truth again. Again and again. Even if I say I already know. Especially if I say I already know.
choices: Promise to tell her as many times as it takes.
Say she deserves to stop wanting to know, just a little.

start.text: The courtyard is full of too much light. Alice sits alone under the tree, her wristwatch open in her hand, taking off the back cover with a tiny screwdriver.

n1.text: I want to give you something. Not the watch. What's inside it. A gear I put back myself on day 3, without ever knowing what for.

n2.text: I found out today. It makes the hand move when someone nearby really wants time to move.

b1.text: Keep it in your inside pocket. If tomorrow the hand moves when you hold it, I'll know the gear has always been yours.

b2.text: I wish time wouldn't pass today. For a few hours. Can it? Just until the sun leaves the tree.

n3.text: It never worked with me. It worked every time you were in the room. It's not science. I know. I wrote that in the margin with an enormous question mark.
choices: Accept the gear and keep it carefully.
Ask what she wants time to do.

start.text: The classroom has a single lantern, on Alice's desk, lit, made of white paper. She stands beside it, her uniform immaculate, the notebook closed.

n1.text: I wrote the last line. I won't say what it is. I'll give it to you closed, for you to open after the roof, or never.

n2.text: I hate open endings. But I learned, this month, that logic doesn't solve everything. That sometimes only the gesture counts.

b1.text: ...Promise. No bargaining. No statistics. Thank you. For the record: it was a good promise.

b2.text: Then I'll have someone to read it with. For the first time, I'll have an audience. I'll be nervous. That's new.

n3.text: So, the gesture: here. Closed. If you come back, I'll have confirmation. And if you don't, I'll know for sure that I trusted you.
choices: Accept the notebook and promise not to open it early.
Say you'll open it as soon as you come down, to read it with her.

start.text: The running track is empty and damp. Hikari runs alone, lap after lap, her steps pounding like a count. When she sees {player_name} in the bleachers, she stops, hands on her knees, breathing hard.

n1.text: I ran forty laps and didn't beat my time. I never need forty laps for that. Something is holding me back.

n2.text: I think it's me. I'm the one holding on. A piece of me is waiting for someone to cross the line beside me and that someone never comes.

b1.text: You're terrible! You're terrible and I loved it. One more. Just one more. I've lost count of the last time I laughed while running.

b2.text: You're staying there? ...Fine. But shout when I pass. Loud. I've been myself in silence for too long.

n3.text: Run with me. One lap. I won't let you win, but I want to know what it's like to run beside someone.
choices: Run a lap with her.
Stay in the bleachers and time her.

start.text: The gym is dark. Hikari is hitting a punching bag hanging from the ceiling, slowly, without force, like someone hitting just to have something to do with her hands.

n1.text: I know I said I'd run until the school was full again. So I ran. And it didn't fill up. My legs are jelly and my head is worse.

n2.text: I hate it when the enemy has no face. I can hit a person. I can't hit a gap.

b1.text: ...Letting someone help. That's all? I thought it was staying on the ground and waiting for it to stop hurting.

b2.text: Okay. Help me up off the ground, then. Pretend I fell.

b3.text: She hits. Once, twice, ten times, harder and harder, until the sound becomes a hoarse breath. At the end, she rests her forehead against the bag and stays there.

b4.text: ...Thanks. I needed to shout at something that wasn't me.

n3.text: Teach me how to lose. I know how to win, I know how to tie, I've never lost properly. I think he knew how to lose and I never asked him how.
choices: Say losing means letting someone help.
Hold the punching bag so she can really hit it.

start.text: At the festival entrance, Hikari waits with her arms crossed, in a hoodie, next to a table where a relay baton rests on a paper towel.

n1.text: It was his. The baton. We never used it in the final. He said I should hold it until he came back from the bathroom. He never came back.

n2.text: I want you to hold it tomorrow. Not for him. For me. Because I want to trust someone with the thing that weighs the most.

b1.text: ...Two hands. You held it like it was glass. No one ever has. It was just a baton.

b2.text: It wasn't just a baton. I know. You can keep it.

b3.text: Run together. We have one baton and two people. That's a math problem. Alice can solve it. I just know I want to.

n3.text: If you drop it, I'll kill you. I mean it. Lovingly, but I mean it.
choices: Hold the baton with both hands.
Say you'd rather run with her than just keep it.

start.text: The lanterns are lighting up one by one. At the bend of the stairs, Hikari stands with one arm against the wall, the other outstretched, like someone holding a door that hasn't opened yet.

n1.text: I'll stay here. At the door. I'll hold it. I said I'd hold it, and I'm good at carrying weight.

n2.text: But if you come back and I'm not here, it's because I ran up after you. Then you wait for me. I'm faster than you, but today I accept losing.

b1.text: Team. That's it. I never had a real one. Just a lane. Go, captain.

b2.text: ...Alice is in the hallway. Yuna, on the stairs. Maya, at the top. I'm holding the door. Everyone is holding something.

b3.text: Okay. Then I'll hold it with everyone. Go.

n3.text: Go. Go before I change my mind and come with you, and the door falls.
choices: Bump your fist against hers, like a team greeting.
Tell her she doesn't have to hold it alone.
